data.title: Constitutive Activation of Skeletal Muscle mTORC1 Drives Pro-Inflammatory Gene Expression in Skeletal Muscle of Aged Mice.
data.authors: Marchant ED; Kalenta H; May J; Lai Z; Salmon AB; Rasmussen BB

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Mouse (inducible skeletal muscle-specific Depdc5 knockout, 27-month-old male mice; dietary rapamycin arm)
data.finding: In 27-month-old mice, inducible loss of Depdc5 (a negative regulator of mTORC1) in skeletal muscle raised inflammatory and immune-related gene expression and TNF-α protein, with shifts in metabolic and angiogenic pathways, but without a change in macrophage phenotype or capillary density. Dietary rapamycin partly reversed mTORC1 signalling and some transcriptional changes, including angiogenesis-related ones, but did not suppress the inflammation-related transcripts or protein. Boundary: one mouse model of genetic, constitutive mTORC1 activation in muscle of very old male mice; it shows that sustained activation is sufficient for these changes in that setting, not that normal age-related mTORC1 activity causes them, and it does not test people or intermittent activity patterns.
data.abstract_excerpt: mTORC1 activity is increased in muscle with aging and is implicated as a potential driver of age-related declines in muscle health. While pharmacological inhibition of mTORC1 improves lifespan and healthspan, it remains unclear whether chronic activation of mTORC1 is sufficient to accelerate aging in skeletal muscle. We aimed to address this question using an inducible model of muscle-specific knockout of Depdc5, which encodes the protein DEP domain containing 5 (DEPDC5), a negative regulator of mTORC1.
